---
title: Create a layer
description: Build your own Pluto layer and plug it into the admin.
navigation:
  icon: i-lucide-package-plus
---

A Pluto layer is a Nuxt layer. It ships source files, and it plugs into the admin with `definePlutoExtension`.

## Layout

A layer has these folders. Use only the ones that you need.

```text
.
├─ app/
│  ├─ assets/css/pluto-layer.css
│  ├─ components/
│  ├─ pages/admin/
│  └─ plugins/pluto-extension.ts
├─ db/migrations/
├─ i18n/locales/
├─ server/
│  ├─ api/
│  └─ plugins/
├─ shared/
│  ├─ types/
│  └─ utils/
└─ nuxt.config.ts
```

## Step 1: the Nuxt config

Name the layer with `$meta.name`. This name is also the extension id and the i18n namespace.

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  extends: [['@plutocms/pluto', { install: true }]],

  $meta: {
    name: 'my-layer'
  }
})
```

Extend only the layers that your layer builds on. Each of them already extends its own upstream layers, so you do not list those again.

| Your layer builds on | Put in `extends` | You get too |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The admin only | `@plutocms/pluto` | `@plutocms/utils` |
| Supabase | `@plutocms/supabase` | `@plutocms/pluto`, `@plutocms/utils` |

For example, `@plutocms/supabase-blog` extends `@plutocms/supabase`, `@plutocms/supabase-storage`, and `@plutocms/ui`. It does not extend `@plutocms/pluto`, because `@plutocms/supabase` already does. Add the layers that you extend to the `dependencies` of the `package.json` of your layer, with a version range.

An app that uses your layer extends only your layer. See [Layers](/core/layers).

::warning
Do not register a `css` entry that imports `tailwindcss` or `@nuxt/ui`. See step 5.
::

### Mark a backend layer

A layer that brings its own backend, such as a database and sign-in, must switch the standalone [GitHub CMS](/github-cms) off. Set `plutoBackend` in `$meta`:

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  $meta: {
    name: 'my-backend',
    plutoBackend: true
  }
})
```

With `plutoCms.enabled: 'auto'` (the default), the CMS stays off and logs nothing. With `plutoCms.enabled: true`, the module logs an error and stays off. The supabase layer, and the `@nuxtjs/supabase` module, count as a backend without this marker.

### Use the local checkouts of other layers

Your layer reads `process.env.PLUTO_<NAME>_PATH || '@plutocms/<name>'` for each layer that it extends. The name is in upper case, with `-` changed to `_`. For `@plutocms/pluto`, the variable is `PLUTO_PLUTO_PATH`. For `@plutocms/supabase-storage`, it is `PLUTO_SUPABASE_STORAGE_PATH`.

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
const plutoLayer = process.env.PLUTO_PLUTO_PATH || '@plutocms/pluto'

export default defineNuxtConfig({
  extends: [plutoLayer]
})
```

An app sets these variables with `PLUTO_LOCAL_ROOT` and the `plutoLayer` helper. See [Local layers](/contributing/workspace#the-plutolayer-helper).

## Step 2: register with `definePlutoExtension`

Call `definePlutoExtension` once, from a plugin, with everything that the layer contributes.

```ts [app/plugins/pluto-extension.ts]
export default defineNuxtPlugin(() => {
  definePlutoExtension({
    id: 'my-layer',
    nav: [
      { id: 'reports', label: 'my-layer.nav.reports', icon: 'lucide:chart-bar', to: '/admin/reports' }
    ],
    pages: [
      { id: 'reports', path: '/admin/reports', title: 'my-layer.nav.reports', icon: 'lucide:chart-bar' }
    ],
    capabilities: [
      { id: 'reports-read', key: 'reports:read', label: 'my-layer.capabilities.reportsRead' }
    ]
  })
})
```

Use a plain `id` for an entry. Use a plain string in `key` for a capability. See [Extension registry](/core/extension-registry) and [Permissions](/core/permissions).

The page file `app/pages/admin/reports.vue` is a normal Nuxt page. Core's admin layout wraps every `/admin/**` page.

Register components of widgets, panels, and banners with `defineAsyncComponent`. See [Lazy loading](/core/lazy-loading).

## Step 3: add a content type

Declare a content type and register it on the client and the server. See [Add a content type](/guides/add-a-content-type).

## Step 4: add text

Put the text of the layer in `i18n/locales/<code>.json`, under one top-level namespace: the `$meta.name` of the layer. Use `pluto.common.*` for shared words.

```json [i18n/locales/en.json]
{
  "my-layer": {
    "nav": { "reports": "Reports" },
    "capabilities": { "reportsRead": "Read reports", "group": "Reports" }
  }
}
```

Registry entries hold keys. Core translates them. Add the same keys to every locale file. See [Internationalization](/core/i18n).

## Step 5: add styles

A layer can ship `app/assets/css/pluto-layer.css`. Core imports it through `#build/pluto.css`.

- Do not import `tailwindcss` or `@nuxt/ui` in it.
- Use only `@theme`, `@custom-variant`, `@utility`, unlayered rules, and imports of plain CSS files next to it.
- Add no `@source` for the `app/` directory. Nuxt UI already scans every layer.
- Use Nuxt UI semantic classes in admin code, such as `bg-default` and `text-muted`.
See [Styles](/core/styles).

## Step 6: add a database migration

A layer on the supabase backend keeps its migrations in `db/migrations/`. Name the files `NNN_slug.sql`. Grant every new table in the same file. See [Migrations](/supabase/migrations) and [Data API grants](/supabase/grants).

## Step 7: publish

A Nuxt layer ships its source. There is no build step for a layer package. Pluto layers use this pipeline:

- Conventional Commits.
- release-please.
- A CI gate.
- npm trusted publishing.

See [Releasing](/contributing/releasing). Set `name`, `version`, `license`, `description`, `publishConfig: { "access": "public" }`, and a `repository` field in `package.json`. npm provenance refuses to publish without the `repository` field.
